Eve CSM: Quick sync — Aurelia Health goes live tomorrow and finance flagged latency spikes during demo. They use heavy streaming+short prompts; renewal in 60 days. Need a customer-facing checklist we can run through with them to reduce cold-start and stabilize cost. Main asks: prefill strategy, batching recommendations, warm pool sizing, and a failback plan. Can we draft one-liner runbook steps for the customer? :thinking:

Maria CS-Ops: +1. I'll sketch a concise runbook for them. High level: 1) turn on tenant warm-pools, 2) prefill top 10 intents at 30m cadence, 3) enable jittered batch window 20-50ms for user-facing routes, 4) streaming fallback to low-cost variant. Will post snippet. :white_check_mark:

Aj SRE: Couple quick Qs — what percentile are the demo spikes at (p95/p99)? also what model size? affects warm pool GPU choices.

Eve CSM: Demo p95 ~ 420ms, p99 spiked to ~1.8s. Using 7B-ish open model (quantized). Customer is on Dedicated trial.

Dan Eng: For the runbook, we usually advise this minimal customer-facing config. Keep it short and copy/paste friendly:

Maria CS-Ops: Posting proposed runbook snippet for customer-facing checklist:

```
1) Prefill: enable tenant_warm_pool = true; prefill_top_intents = ["greeting","search","summary","form_fill","billing"] with cadence = 30m.
2) Warm pool sizing: start with 2 warm slots per 1000 daily active users, increase +1 per additional 500 DAU if p95 > 300ms.
3) Batching: client-side window = 20-50ms; server batch_limit = 64. Use adaptive batching for spikes.
4) Streaming fallback: configure fallback_model = "lighter-7B-q4" and stream_threshold = 800ms.
5) Observability: enable route-level token cost + p95/p99 export to shared dashboard.
6) Escalation: open support runbook with tag #urgent-onboard if p99 > 1.2s for >10m.
```

Maria CS-Ops: Add short note for engineers about prefix caching: TTL 10m for session-level prefixes, extend to 1h for billing prompts.

Aj SRE: Suggestion — for dedicated pools use warm-pool warmup command before business hours: `rbnctl warmup --tenant aurelia --slots 4 --intent-set top10` and run at 4am UTC. Also add a quick test: `curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' https://api.redwood.ai/generate -d '{"prompt": "greeting"}' | jq '.latency'` to validate baseline.

Dan Eng: small caveat: batching window 20-50ms is good, but if their client traffic is very spiky, prefer 10ms with a smaller max batch to keep latency consistent. Put that as an alternative.

Luke PM: From renewal/risk POV: make the checklist customer-facing and include the one-click toggles we can operate if they give permission. If we can get them to accept a short warm-pool trial (2 weeks), that will materially reduce p99. I'll add this to the customer playbook ask for the kickoff.

Eve CSM: Love it. Maria — can you convert the snippet to a one-page PDF I can share in the kickoff call? Also add an internal checklist for us to run post-deploy (smoke tests + dashboard checks).

Maria CS-Ops: On it. Internal post-deploy checklist (short): run prefills, confirm warm slots active, run 5 synthetic requests across top intents, verify p95 < 350ms, p99 < 1s, confirm token cost delta < 12% week-over-week. Will attach the PDF here in the thread when ready. :paperclip:

deploy-bot: scheduled warmup job for tenant aurelia at 2026-03-24T04:00:00Z (4 slots) — created by Maria CS-Ops

Aj SRE: One more operational note — add a safety circuit to auto-scale down warm-pool after 72h of no real user traffic to avoid unnecessary cost.

Eve CSM: Thanks team — this is exactly what I need for the call. I'll share the PDF and ask for the permission to run the warm-pool trial. If they agree, we'll track impact in the renewal health board. :rocket:
